Display the recognized caption line above each translation
Captions appear here while you watch.

Your phone\'s built-in Live Caption turns speech in any video into captions, but it can\'t translate them. This app reads that caption text through an accessibility service and shows the translation in a floating subtitle you can drag anywhere — line for line: whenever Live Caption starts a new line, so does the translation.\n\nFinished lines are translated once and cached; the line still being spoken is refreshed as it grows, so subtitles keep up without flickering.

• Baidu — fastest, free for personal use. Quality is fine for clear speech.

• Qwen-MT — a model built for translation. The best balance of speed and quality.

• DeepSeek / custom — general language models. They see the previous sentences as context, which helps with slang, pronouns and names, at the cost of some latency.
Version %1$s · MIT licensed\nNo analytics, no crash reporting, no servers of our own. API keys stay on this device.

string-array.name: help_steps
string-array.item: Open Settings, pick an engine, enter its key and tap “Test translation”.
Enable the accessibility service. If the toggle is greyed out (sideloaded apps on Android 13+): Settings → Apps → this app → ⋮ → Allow restricted settings, then try again.
Turn on Live Caption: while a video plays, press a volume key and tap the Live Caption icon under the slider — or Settings → Accessibility → Hearing enhancements → Live Caption.
Tap “Start translating”, or turn on Auto-start. Drag the subtitle anywhere; lock it when you want touches to reach the video.

string-array.name: help_faq
string-array.item: The subtitle never shows a translation?
Make sure Live Caption is actually showing captions on screen, and that “Test translation” in Settings succeeds.
It says the key is invalid or out of balance?
Check the key in Settings. DeepSeek and most LLM providers need a positive account balance.
Does it work with Netflix / Disney+?
Yes. The app reads caption text, not the screen, so DRM screenshot blocking doesn\'t apply.
The subtitle blocks the video controls.
Lock the overlay (home screen or Settings) — touches then pass straight through to the app below.
Android 11+ with Google Live Caption: Samsung Galaxy, Pixel and others. Phones without Google Live Caption (most China-market ROMs) won\'t work.
